newsitem.title: USA: Liggett adds 'addictive' warning about cigarettes.
newsitem.headline: Liggett adds 'addictive' warning about cigarettes.

text.p: Brooke Group Ltd, which broke with the tobacco industry last year to settle litigation against it, said Thursday that its Liggett Group unit had added a prominent warning label to L&M cigarettes stating "smoking is addictive."
Liggett, the only U.S. cigarette maker to acknowledge the addictive nature of cigarette smoking, said it began distributing L&M cigarettes with the new label Thursday.
It added that the new warning label also will be placed on its other premium brands -- Chesterfield, Lark and Eve -- and on other cigarettes made and sold by Liggett within 60 days.

The company said the label was part of its previously announced settlement agreements with the attorneys general of 23 states and individual and class-action plaintiffs in legal cases regarding smoking.

"We've moved quickly to honour our commitment to the attorneys general and tobacco plaintiffs to place this important new warning label on our cigarettes," Brooke Group Chairman Bennett LeBow said in a statement.
"We believe warning smokers in clear, unambiguous language is the right thing to do."

The new warning label appears prominently on the front of Liggett's L&M premium cigarette packs, with the legally required Surgeon General's health warning about smoking remaining on the side of the packs.

The development comes amid high-stakes negotiations between other cigarette makers and attorneys general of a number of states over litigation filed against the companies over the health costs of smoking.
Liggett Group, a wholly-owned tobacco subsidiary of Brooke Group based in Durham, N.C., is the fifth-largest manufacturer of cigarettes in the United States in terms of unit sales.
Brooke Group's stock added 25 cents to $44.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
